label: Propositions and quantifiers
summary: A quantifier fixes the universe and the order in which choices may depend on one another.

label: Sets, relations and functions
summary: Functions require a domain, codomain and unambiguous output; relations need not be functions.

label: Induction and recursion
summary: A base case and a justified successor step establish an infinite family without checking every case.

label: Proof obligations and counterexamples
summary: A theorem combines hypotheses, conclusion and a derivation; a single admissible counterexample defeats a universal claim.

label: Dependent types and proof terms
summary: Propositions can be represented as types and proofs as terms checked by a small kernel.

label: Axiom and dependency audit
summary: A proved proposition remains conditional on its actual axioms and dependency statements.

label: Equations and reversible transformations
summary: Division and squaring require domain checks to avoid dropping or adding solutions.

label: Polynomials and factorization
summary: Polynomial structure permits identities, roots and exact arithmetic independent of floating-point approximations.

label: Complex numbers and phase
summary: A complex number combines two real coordinates; multiplication combines scale and angle.

label: Exponentials and logarithms
summary: Logarithms turn multiplication into addition only on the selected domain and branch.

label: Dimensions and nondimensionalization
summary: Every additive term must share dimensions; a nondimensional variable is a ratio to a declared scale.

label: Groups and symmetry
summary: A group records reversible composition, identity and inverses without assuming commutativity.

label: Rings, ideals and quotients
summary: Rings combine addition and multiplication; ideals specify which expressions become equal in a quotient.

label: Fields and extensions
summary: A field permits division by nonzero elements; extensions add algebraic or transcendental elements.

label: Galois correspondence
summary: For finite Galois extensions, subfields and symmetry subgroups correspond in reverse inclusion.

label: Linear representations
summary: A representation turns group composition into matrix multiplication.

label: Lie groups and Lie algebras
summary: Infinitesimal generators organize local continuous symmetries and gauge theory.

label: Commutative algebra
summary: Localization and prime ideals connect polynomial equations with geometric spaces.

label: Vector spaces and linear maps
summary: Linearity means preserving addition and scalar multiplication; coordinates are a choice, not the object.

label: Basis and dimension
summary: A basis gives unique finite coordinate expansions; dimension counts independent directions.

label: Rank and nullspace
summary: The nullspace identifies invisible directions and prevents unjustified inversion.

label: Inner products and norms
summary: An inner product defines lengths and angles, with a conjugate transpose over complex scalars.

label: Determinants and orientation
summary: The determinant measures signed volume scaling of a square linear map.

label: Eigenvalues and spectral theorem
summary: Self-adjoint operators have orthogonal modes; arbitrary matrices need not diagonalize.

label: Singular value decomposition
summary: SVD separates input directions, gains and output directions for rectangular matrices.

label: Pseudoinverse and identifiable subspaces
summary: The pseudoinverse chooses a least-squares solution; it cannot recover an unobserved nullspace.

label: Least squares and projection
summary: Projection minimizes squared error under an explicitly chosen norm.

label: PCA and low-rank compression
summary: PCA captures variance directions, which need not be semantic or causal directions.

label: Tensors and multilinear maps
summary: Tensor rank, matrix rank and the number of stored entries describe different properties.

label: Condition numbers
summary: A stable algorithm cannot remove poor conditioning inherent in the mathematical problem.

label: Limits and continuity
summary: A limit describes controlled approach; sampled agreement does not establish continuity.

label: Derivatives and linearization
summary: The derivative is the local best linear approximation where it exists.

label: Taylor approximation and remainder
summary: A polynomial approximation becomes informative only with a bound on its remainder.

label: Integration and accumulation
summary: Integration accumulates quantities under a declared measure, domain and convergence condition.

label: Chain rule and automatic differentiation
summary: Derivative information propagates through function composition; branch behavior matters.

label: Jacobians and changes of variables
summary: The determinant of a coordinate derivative converts local volume elements.

label: Gradient, divergence and curl
summary: These operators depend on geometry and encode local change, flux and circulation.

label: Divergence theorem
summary: Boundary flux equals integrated interior divergence under regularity and orientation conditions.

label: Stokes theorem
summary: The differential-form theorem unifies several boundary-to-interior identities.

label: Calculus of variations
summary: Stationarity of a functional produces equations plus boundary conditions, not automatically a minimum.

label: Measure and integration
summary: A measure assigns consistent sizes; null sets and almost-everywhere statements differ from pointwise claims.

label: Banach and Hilbert spaces
summary: Completeness permits limits of approximations; Hilbert structure also supplies orthogonal projections.

label: Bounded and unbounded operators
summary: An unbounded operator is specified by its domain as well as its algebraic expression.

label: Holomorphic functions
summary: Complex differentiability imposes stronger constraints than real differentiability.

label: Fourier transforms and distributions
summary: Global frequency coordinates require a convention and a function or distribution class.

label: Sobolev spaces and weak derivatives
summary: Weak derivatives extend differential equations to functions without classical smoothness.

label: Boundary and initial value problems
summary: A differential equation needs data, solution class and a uniqueness/stability question.

label: Heat flow and smoothing
summary: Diffusion damps high-frequency modes, while backward reconstruction can be ill-conditioned.

label: Wave propagation
summary: Wave equations carry finite-speed propagation under appropriate local coefficients.

label: Weak solutions and variational formulations
summary: Testing against smooth functions changes the solution class and requires explicit energy and uniqueness conditions.

label: Distributions and Green functions
summary: A delta is a linear functional on test functions, not an ordinary infinitely high function.

label: Euclidean geometry and metric
summary: Metric information must be distinguished from a coordinate drawing.

label: Manifolds and charts
summary: A manifold is locally Euclidean; one chart rarely describes its entire topology.

label: Tangent spaces and differential forms
summary: Tangents represent velocities; cotangents act on them to give scalar measurements.

label: Riemannian and Lorentzian metrics
summary: A metric measures lengths or intervals and controls index raising and lowering.

label: Connections and covariant derivatives
summary: A connection compares vectors at nearby points; coordinate derivatives alone do not transform correctly.

label: Curvature and holonomy
summary: Curvature measures failure of local transport around infinitesimal loops to commute.

label: Laplace–Beltrami operator
summary: The Laplacian changes with the metric and volume element.

label: Geodesics and variational paths
summary: A geodesic is locally stationary for geometric length or energy and need not be globally shortest.

label: Topological spaces and continuity
summary: Topology records neighborhoods and continuity without requiring lengths.

label: Homotopy and fundamental group
summary: Continuous loop deformation is stronger than mere connectivity in a drawing.

label: Simplicial and cell complexes
summary: Higher-dimensional cells fill some graph cycles, changing which loops represent holes.

label: Homology and boundary maps
summary: Cycles modulo boundaries distinguish persistent holes from locally filled cycles.

label: Cohomology and dual observables
summary: Cohomology evaluates and combines global information carried by local data.

label: Persistent homology
summary: Persistence tracks features across a scale parameter, not proof of their physical meaning.

label: Hodge theory
summary: On suitable manifolds harmonic representatives connect PDEs with topological classes.

label: Graphs, multigraphs and typed edges
summary: Edge direction and type are part of the model; spatial proximity is not an edge.

label: Adjacency and walk counts
summary: Matrix powers count walks with multiplicity, including repeats.

label: Incidence matrices and conservation
summary: A signed incidence matrix expresses how edge flows enter and leave vertices.

label: Graph Laplacians
summary: A Laplacian is a positive semidefinite quadratic energy on an undirected weighted graph.

label: Normalized graph Laplacian
summary: Degree normalization controls the geometry used to compare cuts and random-walk mixing.

label: Graph diffusion and heat kernels
summary: Diffusion smooths a signal across encoded edges and loses high-frequency distinctions.

label: Effective resistance
summary: Resistance measures redundancy of paths under conductance assumptions.

label: Conductance and spectral gaps
summary: A small bottleneck limits mixing and connects combinatorial cuts to eigenvalues.

label: Shortest paths and dynamic programming
summary: Shortest cost depends on edge weights and constraints; it is not strongest evidence.

label: DAGs and topological ordering
summary: A DAG permits prerequisite order; detected cycles need interpretation, not silent truncation.

label: Strongly connected components
summary: Collapsing directed feedback components produces a DAG without pretending the loops disappeared.

label: Counting, extremal sets and Ramsey theory
summary: Existence, constructive algorithms and optimal bounds are distinct questions.

label: Probability spaces and events
summary: Probabilities are conditional on a chosen experiment and model, not inherent truth scores.

label: Random variables and distributions
summary: A random variable is a measurable function, not a sample or a probability density itself.

label: Bayesian conditioning
summary: Updating needs likelihoods and a denominator that can be nonzero; repeated evidence may be dependent.

label: Covariance and correlation
summary: Zero covariance alone does not imply independence.

label: Gaussian models
summary: A covariance matrix must be positive semidefinite; a density needs nonsingular covariance.

label: Concentration inequalities
summary: Bounds depend on independence or other assumptions and cannot be reused after arbitrary selection.

label: Markov chains and stationarity
summary: The Markov property discards history only after choosing a sufficient state.

label: Monte Carlo and sampling error
summary: Variance and dependence determine effective precision; more repeated samples need not mean more independent information.

label: Causal models and interventions
summary: Association graphs do not establish intervention effects without identification assumptions.

label: Shannon entropy
summary: Entropy quantifies a distribution's uncertainty in specified log units.

label: Relative entropy and information gain
summary: KL is directional and can be infinite when support is missing.

label: Mutual information
summary: Information shared statistically is not the same as a causal mechanism.

label: Regularization and inverse problems
summary: A penalty stabilizes solutions by introducing a modeling preference.

label: Generalization and evaluation
summary: Performance must be measured on the intended distribution with contamination controls.

label: Embeddings and metric learning
summary: A learned vector geometry is an approximation tied to model, objective and training data.

label: Floating-point arithmetic
summary: Finite precision makes operation order important and can destroy naive cancellation.

label: Root finding and Newton iteration
summary: Newton is locally powerful but can diverge or converge to an unintended root.

label: Convex and nonconvex optimization
summary: The feasible domain and curvature determine whether a stationary point is globally optimal.

label: Gradient descent and step sizes
summary: Step size and smoothness control descent; a large learning rate can cause oscillation.

label: Lagrange duality and KKT conditions
summary: Dual variables can certify bounds, with constraint qualifications needed for equality of optima.

label: Conjugate gradients and preconditioning
summary: CG exploits SPD structure; preconditioning changes the geometry of convergence.

label: Finite differences
summary: Consistency must be paired with stability and boundary treatment.

label: Finite elements and weak forms
summary: Basis functions approximate a variational solution while respecting boundary constraints.

label: Numerical quadrature
summary: Smoothness and sampling placement determine error; highly oscillatory integrands need specialized treatment.

label: Contractions and fixed points
summary: A contraction supplies existence, uniqueness and a quantitative stopping certificate.

label: Computational complexity and reductions
summary: A theorem about Turing machines, word RAM or arithmetic circuits must retain that model.

label: Linear programming
summary: LP optimality and algorithmic complexity are separate properties.

label: Primes and unique factorization
summary: Prime factorization translates multiplication into exponents, while computation can remain hard.

label: Zeta and L-functions
summary: Analytic continuation and zero locations connect complex analysis with arithmetic.

label: Elliptic curves
summary: A nonsingular genus-one curve with a chosen point admits a geometric group law.

label: Modular and automorphic forms
summary: Automorphy constrains analytic functions under arithmetic group actions.

label: Schemes and sheaves
summary: Local rings and gluing preserve algebraic structure that point sets alone lose.

label: Langlands correspondences
summary: Different Langlands programs require different precise statements and are not interchangeable.

label: Categories and composition
summary: Objects, morphisms and their lawful composition give a language for comparisons across subjects.

label: Functors and structure preservation
summary: A functor must preserve identities and composition, not merely pair similar-looking objects.

label: Natural transformations
summary: Naturality requires a commuting relation for every relevant morphism.

label: Universal properties and limits
summary: A construction is characterized by how all admissible maps factor through it.

label: Yoneda and representability
summary: An object is characterized, up to isomorphism, by its relationships expressed through hom-functors.

label: All mathematical problems have been solved
summary: No. A catalogue or benchmark cannot establish universal mathematical solvability.
